reviewer_role: Independent reader of the shear-strengthening proofs; author of the separately reviewed native implementation.
proof_checks: The diagonal mismatch image and the core-crossing image are injective and disjoint: their matrix entries lie on the diagonal and in the lower-left block, respectively.
The smaller core side has size at least (d-q)/2; expansion and eta <= 2 yield eta*d <= 2*(q+e), proving the sharper nonzero-count bound.
Actual row/column support <= Delta+1 and the basis-row rank lemma imply max crossing rank >= eta*d/[4*(Delta+1)^2], including characteristic two.
The arbitrary-law linear-fiber argument scales crossing rank by the full bit-lane width and subtracts exactly the source entropy deficit.
Every positive-mass helper fiber receives its normalized conditional law; zero-mass fibers contribute zero and need no nonemptiness hypothesis.
Independent within-row recodings preserve the relevant observation fibers, while cross-row changes of representation remain outside the hypothesis.
Each branch has two recovery states bounded by the same branch budget; the max conditional entropy is bounded by that budget and averaged exactly.
The new charge is P-H(X|Z), equivalent to D_X+I(X;Z), for arbitrary finite joint laws. No condition Z=f(X) or independence is imposed.
Arbitrary ambient state types are restricted to their actual finite ranges without introducing a rounding loss.
All original bounds are preserved as weaker corollaries; their exact source headers remain unchanged.
